meeting_flow.opening_phrase: I thought I'd start just by understanding a bit more on your current sort of situation. I understand you're looking to buy a property, is that right?
rapport_topics: Lindsay in the middle of building works at her home property
meeting_flow.pivot_to_business: All right, so I would assume we— well, I think what we should probably do, we can go through some of the figures and then our service, see if it sort of lines up with what you're looking for.
meeting_flow.income_intro: So we're looking at about £71,500 of revenue, about just under £6,000 per month. Which that translates roughly into what you can expect as a payout each month of about £3,100 or £37,000 a year.
meeting_flow.how_it_works_transition: Our next part I suppose is, you know, what do you get for that sort of service? What does it look like for you? What do we cover? What's left for you?
meeting_flow.pre_close_setup: sometimes lenders will ask to want information from like a shortlet or like a management company to sort of pass their lending requirements. When it comes to that point, if they ask for that, just let me know.
meeting_flow.close_phrase: What I can probably do following this call is I can send you like a summary of everything we've spoken about and all the information into like an action plan.
meeting_flow.meeting_2_ask: Yeah, I'd say give me a call back this time next week. I will hopefully be in a position to say we're moving forward and offers have been accepted.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Tell me a bit more about your company.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Short-let management company started with business partner Martin; own Airbnbs for about 6 years; built the management because he wasn't getting the service or information he needed from the management companies he used.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: How did you arrive at that nightly rate and the overall gross? So I've had a couple of other estimates that come in much lower.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Based on 12 comparables of similar spec; 3 nearby properties doing more; caveat that comparables have months or years of reviews so expect 10-15% less for up to a year until momentum builds.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: And you say it's not competitive. Is that simply because there isn't the supply of stock?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Rural, not a built-up area, so low competition; most money made in April to August over 5 or 6 months, with January-March and September-December quiet and a small December spike.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: That's fine because we plan to use the property ourselves, so that's fine.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Just talk me through your fees again though, if you wouldn't mind. ... Do you take the booking platform fees off first and then charge your fees?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: 15% plus VAT of gross bookings, which comes in after booking platform fees.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Are there any restrictions? Because I know some of the booking sites and agents have restrictions on the amount of time owners can spend at the property.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: No, you can stay as often as you like as long as no guest is booked; just tell us via the Slack channel when you block dates.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Yeah, sure. Yeah, that's reasonable. Fair enough.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: I'm really keen to hear about your experience. ... What were your priorities in terms of service? And how have you then built that into your offering to other clients?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Could see reviews but had no way to speak to anyone when things went south, just generic email replies; relied on the manager for regulation updates. Built vetting of cleaners and guests, a Slack channel for communication and regulation updates, and optional review calls every 3 months.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: if we could rent it out at even 50% occupancy rather than 60% occupancy, that would be good enough for me ... it'd be nice if it washed its face
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Yeah, yeah, I understand, I understand. Okay.
